Part 1

How often does a protection layer fail when needed?

Part 1 · the plan

From failure rate to the PFD of a whole SIF

  1. Rate to probabilitywhy the average PFD is $\lambda T/2$
  2. Proof testingthe saw-tooth and the test interval
  3. Blocks in series and in parallelRBD rules
  4. The CR-201 SIFswhich component dominates

Step 1 · exponential failures

A hidden failure waits for the next test

$$PFD(t) = 1-e^{-\lambda t}\approx \lambda t,\qquad PFD_{avg}=\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \lambda t\,dt=\frac{\lambda T}{2}$$

$\lambda$ failures per year, $t$ time since the last test, $T$ test interval in years.

Constant $\lambda$: failures arrive at randomuseful-life part of the bathtub
$\lambda t \ll 1$, so $1-e^{-\lambda t}\approx\lambda t$first term of the series
A proof test resets PFD to zero every $T$average over one interval

Step 2 · interactive · rate and test interval

Halve the test interval, halve the PFD

From step 1$PFD_{avg}=\lambda T/2$
$PFD_{avg}$
band

XV-101 with its solenoid, 0.024 /yr tested yearly: PFDavg 0.012, SIL 1 on the valve alone.

Step 3 · reliability block diagrams

Series adds; parallel multiplies

$$PFD_{SIF}\approx\sum_i PFD_i,\qquad PFD_{1oo2}\approx\frac{(\lambda T)^2}{3},\qquad PFD_{1oo2,\ diverse}\approx\frac{\lambda_1\lambda_2T^2}{3}$$

$PFD_i$ of each block; $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ rates of two different sensors.

Series: any block fails the SIF; 1oo2: both channels must failno common cause in this tab

Step 4 · interactive · pick a SIF

The shut-off valve dominates every SIF

$PFD_{avg}$
band

XV with its solenoid gives 0.012 of about 0.02: test the valve more often, or add a second one.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • A hidden failure is found only by a proof test.
  • $PFD_{avg}=\lambda T/2$ for one channel.
  • In series the PFDs add; in 1oo2 they multiply.
  • Every CR-201 SIF sits in SIL 1, set by the valve.

Each layer now has a number. Next: multiply them along a scenario.

Part 2

Does each scenario meet its target frequency?

Part 2 · the plan

One equation, four scenarios

  1. The LOPA equationcause to consequence frequency
  2. Targets and creditsseverity criteria, typical IPL PFDs
  3. IPL rulesindependent, specific, in time
  4. The CR-201 worksheetfour scenarios, today and with fixes

Step 1 · one scenario, one line

Frequency falls by each layer's PFD

$$f_C = \sum_{\text{causes}} f_{IE}\cdot P_{enab}\cdot\prod_j PFD_j\cdot \prod_k CM_k,\qquad RRF=\frac{f_C}{f_T}$$

$P_{enab}$ enabling probability, $CM_k$ conditional modifiers; frequencies per year.

$RRF\le 1$ tolerable; $RRF>1$: add a layer with $PFD\le 1/RRF$or remove the cause

Step 2 · the course criteria

Worse consequences demand rarer events

Step 3 · when a safeguard earns credit

No credit without independence and time

RuleFails on CR-201 when
Independent of the causeLIC-201 HI alarm, when LT-201 reads low
Specific to the consequenceSSLL-201 trip: it does not stop the settling
Effective in timeFIC-302 LO alarm: tubes boil in 34 s
Not shared with another IPLFSLL-302 and FIC-302 on one FT-302
Auditable, testableProcedures: a safeguard, never an IPL

Step 4 · interactive · pick a scenario, switch layers

The LOPA worksheet, cause by cause

Overpressure misses its target by a factor of 105 today: R01, LR1 and LR2 bring it inside.

Step 4 · interactive · today or with the recommendations

Three of four scenarios need new layers

Only the heater scenario meets its target today; every scenario does once the recommended layers are fitted.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • $f_C$ multiplies the cause by every credited PFD.
  • Targets fall a decade per severity level.
  • A shared sensor or too little time removes the credit.
  • Overpressure, overfill and restart need new layers.

LOPA takes one path at a time. Next: the bow-tie shows them all.

3

Part 3

What does the bow-tie add, and is there time to act?

Part 3 · the plan

Threats, barriers, escalation and time

  1. Bow-tie anatomyprevention left, mitigation right
  2. A bow-tie labrecommended barriers and escalation factors
  3. Time to actalarm credit against model runs

Step 1 · CR-201 overpressure

One top event, many paths in and out

Threats and prevention barriers on the left; the top event in the centre; mitigation barriers and consequences on the right. Escalation factors defeat barriers.

Step 2 · interactive · fit barriers, add escalation

An escalation factor can undo a barrier

With R01 fitted the fatality case meets its target; a relief inlet blocked by crystals puts it ten times over.

Step 3 · interactive · pick an alarm

Alarm credit needs about ten minutes

Overfill leaves 35 min and the heater 34 s: the same alarm type earns credit on one and not the other.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • A bow-tie shows every threat and consequence of one top event.
  • Escalation factors can remove a barrier's credit.
  • Model runs decide whether an alarm earns credit.

The SIFs now have targets. Next: the SRS of SIF tab specifies them.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

$PFD_{avg}=\lambda T/2$: test interval is a design variable.

2

Credit only layers that are independent, specific and in time.

3

CR-201 overpressure misses its target 105-fold until relief is fitted.

4

Check every alarm credit against the process safety time.
